sessions.name: RACE: IRONMAN Hamburg
sessions.description: PLANNING 9:07, stretch 8:40. Swim 1:10 / bike 4:51 @ 201 W NP (IF 0.76 of the latest tested FTP -- if the test says less, ride less) / run 3:02 @ 4:19/km, first 10 km 10 s/km slower. Bike 85-95 g/h from the CHO bottle plus water, run 60-75 g/h, nothing new; in-race rescue if the gut turns. On 2026 numbers the M40-44 qualifying line was a ~9:21 finish: race the plan.

rationale:
Wolsztyn 2026 (4:38:21) was a fueling result, not a fitness one: the bike was correctly ridden (208 W NP = IF 0.83 on the planning 250 W FTP, VI 1.03, 4.3% decoupling in 15 km/h wind) and the run fell from 4:02/km to 5:03/km with HR FALLING -- no substrate, not an aerobic limit.
Demonstrated full distance is 10:27:00 (Malbork 2025). The planning line for Malbork 2027 is 9:17 and for Hamburg 2028 is 9:07; 8:50 and 8:40 are held as optimistic stretch targets. Where the planning minutes come from, against 2025: swim 1:20 -> 1:12 (cold/OW skill; 1:09 would be 11-13 min), bike 5:19 -> 4:56 (disc + deep front, FTP 245 -> 258 at the same IF 0.76), run 3:47 -> 3:04 (a weekly threshold session and 55-70 km/week instead of 35-45). The stretch lines additionally need CdA ~0.03-0.04 better, which only the aero test can confirm.
2027 is a racing year on an honest engine: autumn strength, swim technique and threshold work into November, then winter threshold and VO2 runs, spring volume into Sieraków (B), then Syców (B) as the fueling dress rehearsal and seven IM-specific weeks into Malbork. Winter 2027-28 moves the emphasis to the limiters 2027 exposes: run volume and threshold, cold/open-water skill and gut capacity. Spring 2028 is IM-specific with a tune-up 70.3 five weeks out and a Mujika taper (>=40% off the peak over the final 14 days) -- the same shape as Malbork's.
Swim >=3/week and run >=4/week throughout. Monday is a genuine rest day.
